values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/lakemargrethe ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Lake Margrethe State Forest Campground, Crawford: 37 sites, $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Developed boat launch at the south side of the campground; lakefront picnic area with four tables at the north end; carry-in access straight from some sites.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/lakemargrethe ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.' 'A developed boat launch is located on Lake Margrethe.' values.note: First-come only, but registration is now by phone or online (using the number or website posted at the campground), no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival; the site must then be set up and occupied. No advance payments or reservations.

values.note: 37 sites 'for tent, small trailer and large trailer use' (no maximum length posted). Nine of them are walk-in sites a short hike (10-30 yards) from a designated trailhead: #1-3, 29-32, 34 and 36, numbered within the 37 the amenity table counts. One camping unit and six people per site.

note: Rustic state forest campground in heavy woods on Lake Margrethe, 6.6 mi W of Grayling via M-72, McIntyres Landing Rd, Regimental Way and Euclid Ave (Crawford County); managed by Hartwick Pines State Park. Most sites have direct lake access; the Manistee and Au Sable rivers are close by for canoeing and fishing. DNR advisory (2026): MDHHS fish-consumption guidelines for PFOS and a warning not to swallow foam on Lake Margrethe, as high PFAS levels may be present. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 37 sites for tent, small and large trailers, 9 of them walk-in (count 46 -> 37: the 9 walk-ins are numbered within the 37), $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only (now registered by phone/online from 8 a.m. on arrival day), 15-day maximum (all confirmed, registration note new). Season (open all year, roads not plowed) already manual and matches the page. Boat launch, picnic area, PFAS advisory. Not equestrian (type 'rustic'). Note trimmed of field restatements.
